bullets.title: META: +32.7% MTD on Muse AI launch, strongest month since 2013; vol surface compressing
bullets.body: META has surged ~32.7% in September—its best monthly gain since 2013—driven by the new Muse AI app launch and partnership with Shopify (SHOP +7.3% on the tie-up). Fixed-strike vol is compressing today, which is negative for long call holders, and one trader flags a secondary offering as a risk that could cap the rally.

bullets.title: NVDA: Ascending triangle breakout eyed; long-dated IV cheapening on rally
bullets.body: NVDA is potentially breaking out of an ascending triangle with the 61.8% Fibonacci level cleared and the 76.4% level (~$2,034) as next resistance. Across the 3–18-month vol surface, implied vol is declining even as the stock rallies, making longer-dated options relatively cheap. Separately, Korean media reports Nvidia has asked South Korea, Japan, and Taiwan substrate makers to complete glass substrate development by 2028.

bullets.title: MU: $15M whale call buy, breakout with $1,200 PT cited; 2GB GDDR7 chip discontinued
bullets.body: A large buyer purchased ~$15M in short-dated MU calls, and the stock is described as breaking out with a $1,200 price target. On the product side, Micron is discontinuing its 2GB GDDR7 chip (D8FHL, 28Gbps) used in GeForce RTX 50 series, shifting focus to denser 3GB GDDR7 for AI and premium GPU segments; RTX 50 will now rely solely on Samsung/SK Hynix for GDDR7 supply.

bullets.title: AMD: Strong call flow; sentiment surged 166% ahead of 9.95% move, $1T mkt cap achieved
bullets.body: AMD is described as bouncing off its 50-day moving average with bullish momentum, and Stocktwits sentiment reportedly surged 166% ahead of a 9.95% stock gain that pushed AMD to a $1T+ market cap. Institutional buyers have been accumulating QQQ and AMD calls non-stop through the week.

bullets.title: AAPL: Screenless fitness tracker in development; $5T market cap reclaimed; AI Mac strategy
bullets.body: Apple is working on a screenless, wrist-worn fitness tracker (à la WHOOP) in development for several months, per Bloomberg. Apple's market cap crossed $5T again. Separately, Apple is launching new AI-focused Mac models positioned as a cost-competitive alternative to Microsoft/Nvidia for AI computing, and analysts note an opportunity for a cheaper Mac desktop given the $900 Mac Mini starting price.

bullets.title: AMZN: AWS wins first-ever NATO Restricted Cloud approval; Trump disclosed up to $25M sale in July
bullets.body: AWS became the first cloud provider cleared for NATO Restricted (NR) workloads across all NATO member nations. On the political front, Trump disclosed selling up to $25M each of MSFT and AMZN on July 20, part of 1,156 trades totaling ~$270M in July. Separately, Stratechery notes Amazon is blocking Muse and discusses Amazon's competitive moat.

bullets.title: MSFT: Trump sold up to $25M in July; Xbox cuts jobs, studios folded into Activision; gaming retreat
bullets.body: Trump disclosed selling up to $25M of MSFT in July. On the business side, Microsoft is cutting hundreds of Xbox jobs and transferring game studios (including Obsidian, folded into Bethesda/Rare) under Activision as the Xbox reset deepens—analysts characterize this as a further retreat from the Xbox brand.

bullets.title: TSLA: Grok Bot officially launches in Tesla vehicles; Grok 4.7 performing engineering work
bullets.body: Grok Bot has officially launched in Tesla vehicles, enabling complex task automation (ordering, reservations, scheduling). Elon Musk separately highlighted that Grok 4.7 is performing real engineering work at Tesla.

bullets.title: SHOP: +7.3% on Muse AI partnership with Meta; catalyst for AI-linked tech rotation into Nasdaq record
bullets.body: Shopify jumped 7.3% following the announcement of its Muse AI partnership with Meta, leading a rotation out of financials into AI-linked tech. The move helped push the Nasdaq 100 toward its first record close since June.

bullets.title: SNDK: +1z score momentum; author sees upside through 2027
bullets.body: SNDK is trading at its highest statistical score (+1z) in an extended period, with the author predicting continued upside through 2027. Broader data center and memory infrastructure exposure is described as showing a 'broad upward inflection' in GS Factor Dashboard.

bullets.title: LITE: OCS market experience a moat, but growth ≠ guaranteed durable revenue
bullets.body: LITE currently benefits from manufacturing expertise and customer-qualification experience in the OCS (optical compute switching) market, but analysts note that market growth alone does not automatically translate to durable revenue or market share for suppliers.

bullets.title: PLTR: Trump's portfolio manager disclosed day-trading Palantir in July filings
bullets.body: Trump's July periodic transaction report (1,156 total trades disclosed) shows the portfolio manager actively day-trading PLTR. Palantir is described as a major defense contractor holding in the filing. Separately, Palantir exec Chad Wahlquist argued copying Palantir is the most counter-productive thing competitors can do.

bullets.title: NFLX: HSBC cuts to Hold
bullets.body: HSBC downgraded Netflix to Hold; no price target disclosed in the headline.

bullets.title: ABNB/CART: Airbnb expands grocery delivery with Instacart across US and Canada
bullets.body: Airbnb announced an expansion of its grocery delivery service partnership with Instacart, available across the US and Canada. Guests can order groceries through the Airbnb app ahead of their stays.

bullets.title: APP vs U: APP's 77.7% operating margin vs Unity's re-acceleration in focus
bullets.body: A detailed analysis compares AppLovin (77.7% operating margin) and Unity Software across growth, margins, FCF, and competitive positioning, examining whether Unity's re-acceleration can challenge APP's dominant profitability profile.

bullets.title: GS desk: subdued activity; semis and macro products net for sale; software shorts elevated
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs mid-day desk note flags overall activity at 3/10. Long-only accounts -10% better for sale led by macro products and semis; hedge funds -8% better for sale; noticeable increase in software short activity today.

bullets.title: Semi/AI infra sector leadership intact; SMH failed bear flags suggest upside thrust
bullets.body: Technology remains the clear market leader with strength concentrated in fiber optics, semiconductors, data storage, and networking. SMH bear flag attempts over the past several weeks have all failed and converted to upside thrusts, with the latest setup described as especially strong. MicroLED is gaining traction in AI interconnect discussions (Avicena shipping 1Tbps eval kits), relevant for optical interconnect names.

bullets.title: Fed hawkish signals: Collins, Barkin support last week's hike; 50/50 odds on next move
bullets.body: Fed's Collins flagged increased likelihood of scenarios where inflation stays notably above 2%, advocating for a somewhat more restrictive fed funds rate. Barkin also supported the hike, noting inflation risks outweigh employment risks, though he hopes for a 1990s-style mid-cycle adjustment. Market now pricing a 50/50 split between a hike and a hold at the next meeting.

bullets.title: NVDA/AI: Jensen Huang at G20 says gigawatt AI factory costs $50–60B; Alibaba launches rival AI chip
bullets.body: Jensen Huang told G20 ministers that a gigawatt-scale AI factory requires $50–60B in capex, emphasizing balance of specialization and flexibility. Separately, Alibaba unveiled the Zhenwu V900, claiming it is China's most powerful AI chip, backed by a $53B investment program with clusters of 500,000 GPUs—a potential competitive threat to NVDA dominance in China AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: Texas data center moratorium escalates to halt; macro headwind for AI infrastructure build-out
bullets.body: Texas Governor escalated from a moratorium to a full halt on new data centers, adding regulatory risk to AI infrastructure expansion in the state. Analysts tracking 400+ local moratoriums note 20GW is inside live moratorium boundaries, though only ~1.5GW faces actual delays given existing permits, vested rights, and equipment lead times.
